item.title: Europa estudia crear un protocolo de seguridad para enfrentar los ataques híbridos de Rusia Los ministros de Defensa de la Unión Europea comenzaron a estudiar este lunes la creación de un nuevo Protocolo de Emergencia para responder de forma coordinada a amenazas y ataques híbridos, especialmente los atribuidos a Rusia. La jefa de la diplomacia europea, Kaja Kallas, explicó que el mecanismo se aplicaría ante agresiones que no lleguen al nivel de un ataque armado, como sabotajes, ciberataques o acciones en la llamada “zona gris”. La propuesta busca complementar, y no sustituir, los mecanismos de defensa colectiva de la OTAN y de la propia Unión Europea. | DW Español

item.title: Meteor hit Oklahoma 100 million years later than previously thought
item.description: Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin have rewritten a small part of Oklahoma's geologic history with global implications for ancient life. item.title: Mapping the 'social network' of proteins in the cell to understand how genes shape living things
item.description: One of biology's fundamental questions is how our genes shape who we are. Adrian Serohijos and Stephen Michnick, professors in the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Medicine at Université de Montréal's Faculty of Medicine, are studying the relationship between genotype and phenotype—that is, how DNA becomes RNA, then protein, and ultimately gives rise to observable characteristics in an individual or any other living organism. "We're trying to unravel the mechanisms of the genome, specifically how the information it encodes is processed inside the cell," Serohijos says. Fuente: Phys.org.
